text:
Arber Xhekaj has become one of the more talked-about players in Montreal this month, and not only for the fighting. The Montreal Gazette wrote about him blossoming on the blue line and asked why referees seem to be targeting him, The Hockey Writers wrote the NHL has him under surveillance, and Sportsnet's Eric Engels wrote about his evolution. Andrew Berkshire of Game Over Network said watching him skate the puck out has been one of his favourite new things about the Habs this season.

The numbers back up the improvement, modestly. In about 12 minutes a night, Montreal takes 52% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, a little better than without him. That's a real change from last season, when Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level and in the bottom 2% of defensemen for creating offense. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 15% of the entries aimed at him, above the typical 11%.

He has four points in 19 games and 37 hits, and his brother Florian has joined him in the lineup. Our talent range has him around 12 points. With Mike Matheson hurt, he may get more minutes than usual.
